submitter: bugs_open/333 lane — policy routability at the door (2026-08-24)
rationale:
bugs_open/333: ~26 producers file content findings at handler_agent='page-build-handler' and none of them, nor the shared writeWorkItem seam most pass through, reads pages.rebuild_policy. A finding on a rebuild_policy='owned' page is therefore routed at the one handler forbidden to touch it. Since bugs_closed/301 the refusal is cheap, but the OUTCOME is the defect: the item terminates 'wont_fix' — the status meaning 'we decided not to fix this' — on a page with a real detector-found defect; idx_swi_dedup excludes wont_fix so the detector re-files it; and the only human-visible trail (owned_page_review) dedups per PAGE, so the SECOND distinct finding on an already-reviewed page leaves no trace at all. [MEASURED 2026-08-24 14:15Z, live table] 83 findings ended that way since 2026-08-19, five of them that day, the most recent at 11:48Z. This is the untaken fix candidate 3 of TWO closed files (bugs_closed/295, bugs_closed/301) and the owner filed it as its own bug on 2026-08-19 (decision (a)).

THE FIX is candidate 1: a policy check at the shared write door, beside the registration check bugs_open/291 already put there. Three design decisions the council should weigh:

(1) THE DOOR READS THE HANDLER'S OWN DECLARATION, NOT A GO LIST OF NAMES. page-build-handler opts into refusing owned pages through config (migration 488 sets refuse_owned_page on its load_page_record step). A Go slice of handler names would be another hand-kept copy of a fact the DB holds, and wrong in the dangerous direction the day a handler opts in. Positive control, and it could have come out otherwise: [MEASURED 2026-08-24] exactly ONE live agent declares it (page-build-handler), while page-rerender (5,040 completions on owned pages, live+archive), section-editor (44 complete/1 failed) and tool-generator (43) do not — which is what makes them safe to leave alone.

(2) THE PARKED ROW KEEPS ITS OWN item_type AND item_key, taking only bugs_closed/077's SIGNAL (status='deferred', empty handler, gap_kind, builder_needed). The first draft followed 077 literally and re-typed the row to capability_gap. That was WRONG and a red-team pass caught it before any code was written: detectors retract their own findings via resolveWorkItems, which matches (item_type, item_key), and 'deferred' is NOT in workItemClosedStatuses — so a row keeping its identity IS retracted normally when the page is later repaired, whereas a re-typed one would sit at deferred for ever holding its dedup slot, undispatchable and un-refilable at once. That is the exact hole two council seats caught on bugs_open/342 one day earlier. Keeping the key also delivers the bug's stated requirement — counted PER FINDING, not per page — for free. The roadmap sweep (diagnose_triage_action.go:355-365, fixloop_digest_action.go:358) reads '(item_type=capability_gap OR status=deferred)' grouped by builder_needed, so the consumer still sees it.

(3) 'deferred', NOT 'blocked' AND NOT 'needs_human_review'. blocked self-heals — feasibility-recheck promotes any blocked row whose handler exists, every 600s, wiping error. needs_human_review holds 1,087 rows and the owner has ruled that queue should not fill (bugs_open/033). deferred is the estate's parking state: nothing promotes it, it holds its dedup slot so the detector cannot churn, and it already has a reader.

SCOPE HONESTY: this does NOT repair owned pages. It converts 'silently refused and forgotten' into 'visibly parked with its reason and the route that does work'. What repairs an owned page is bugs_open/277's question and the owner ruled 08-19 that the two must not be merged. Nine raw-INSERT writers bypass the seam (admin handlers, tool guide pages, write_audit_findings) — for those the handler's own cheap refusal remains the backstop, exactly as claim's branch is 291's. Named, not silently dropped.

plan.summary: Park a content finding at 'deferred' with no handler, keeping its item_type/item_key, when its page is rebuild_policy='owned' AND its handler declares refuse_owned_page — checked once at the shared writeWorkItem door instead of in ~26 producers. Ships ARMED with a redeploy-free kill switch.

edits.rationale: One definition of the declaration predicate, in the package that already owns the routability renderer (import direction: actions imports discovery_checks, never the reverse). A scalar subquery, not an EXISTS, because the question is the VALUE of a config property, not the existence of a row — and it is deliberately NOT the registration predicate, which work_item_routability_single_definition_test.go requires to have exactly one definition.

Thin delegation (mirroring workItemHandlerRegisteredSQL) plus the status set the door triggers on. workItemStatusHeadsForDispatch is a NEW function, not a widening of workItemStatusRequiresRegisteredHandler: widening that one demotes the flag-only findings to blocked, which is bugs_closed/284's regression and is pinned by 291's own test. 'detected' is IN the new set and OUT of the old because registration is re-judged at promotion (WDS-017) while ownership is re-judged by NOBODY.

Extract the ownership SQL so a caller holding a *sql.Tx runs the SAME statement inside its own transaction — the file's 'ONLY place a pipeline may read ownership policy' comment stays literally true. It returns the ERROR rather than a checked bool because the two callers want opposite things from ErrNoRows: the composition guards treat any error as unreadable (ERROR log, counted), while the door treats a page that does not resolve as 'not owned' (a work item can legitimately carry a stale spec.page_id). The nil check stays in the *sql.DB wrapper, before boxing, to avoid the typed-nil trap.

edits.rationale: The door itself, plus the pure transform. It runs FIRST, before the anti-churn brake: the item_key's history is full of this finding's own refusals (112 failed rows on owned pages at that handler), so brake-first would brand the third refusal '[unresolved after 2 attempts]' — terminal, slot freed — before the door ever saw a dispatchable status. 291's registration block runs after both and correctly skips a 'deferred' row. Probe order is declaration-first so the common case pays one indexed lookup and never reads pages. Demote, never refuse (291's rule): discovery sweeps log-and-continue on insert error, so a refusal here loses the finding to a pod log. The error column reuses the existing conditional extraCols/argN append, so the 16-arg callers stay byte-identical.

Mutation-proven both ways: disarming the door fails the positives; re-typing/re-keying the parked row fails the retraction-contract assertions (both run, both caught). Discriminating negative: an owned page at page-rerender (the 5,040-completion route) is untouched. THE TRAP THIS FILE DOCUMENTS: the door fails open, so sqlmock's unexpected-query error is swallowed and a test that omits the probe expectations passes having proved nothing. Instrumenting the door found 21 such cases across 8 existing files; all are re-scripted here via two shared helpers, and every discriminating negative calls ExpectationsWereMet.

edits.rationale: Producer honesty (bugs_open/177's lesson: a producer whose metric counts a FILING as success reports 100% while filing items unsatisfiable at birth). Two additive result keys beside the existing born_blocked, so a config-driven producer can tell 'filed and dispatchable' from 'filed and parked' without a second query. handler_agent keeps reporting what the CONFIG asked for — that is the contract every existing consumer reads.

withWorkItemTx collapses the write outcome to a bool, so a producer cannot see a park. Added as a SIBLING that returns the full workItemWrite, with the bool version delegating — a widened signature would land this change in the diffs of three files owned by other lanes for no benefit to them.

The tool pipeline is the LARGEST single producer of owned-page findings at page-build-handler (57 of ~260 lifetime, the bug's census): it asks the generic builder for prose around a widget on a page the same pipeline marked owned. That design conflict is the bug's fix candidate 2 and belongs to the tool lane — not taken here. What IS taken: the step result stops calling the filing a raise, because 'raised' is what made this class look healthy while nothing happened.

plan.risks:
PARKING SOMETHING REPAIRABLE. If a handler declared refuse_owned_page but could in fact repair owned pages, the door would park findings that would have been fixed. Bounded by the declaration being the handler's own opt-in (it refuses at load_page_record today, so the park changes the record, not the outcome), and by the kill switch. The failure direction to watch is the declaration query returning a handler that does NOT refuse — the RUNBOOK names it.

THE PROBES RUN INSIDE THE CALLER'S TRANSACTION. Fail-open covers driver/context/scan errors; a server-side SQL error aborts the tx and the INSERT fails with it, which no fall-through can undo. The comment says this rather than claiming a safety the code lacks; the jsonpath literal is pinned by a parity test against migration 488 and was verified against the live estate.

'deferred' IS OFF THE ADMIN ATTENTION QUEUES. site_admin_handlers.go's retry/resolve lists are needs_human_review/failed/blocked/(triaged)/unresolved — a parked high-severity finding is visible to the roadmap sweep and the OWNED_PAGE_GUARD marker query, not to those. Stated in the register entry; it is the same posture 077's 45 live rows already have.

COUNTING REGRESSION FOR EXISTING QUERIES. A census of 'error LIKE OWNED_PAGE_GUARD%' now counts parked rows alongside handler refusals. A LANDMINE entry and a dated correction to the 301 lane's NOTES query say to add AND status <> 'deferred'.

THE 9 RAW-INSERT WRITERS BYPASS THE DOOR (admin handlers, deploy_tool/create_tool_component guide pages, create_blog_posts, apply_adoption_plan, write_audit_findings). Backstop unchanged; listed by path in the register entry so the set is enumerable rather than folklore.

LEGACY ROWS ARE UNTOUCHED. 142 open rows (59 failed/36 unresolved/16 needs_human_review) still hold the old handler; the post-roll verification splits by created_at vs roll time precisely so their continued refusals are not read as the fix failing.
